battle.name: 納拉姆辛對盧盧比的行動
battle.theater: 美索不達米亞北部扎格羅斯山麓
battle.brief: 前二二三〇年，阿卡德王國的國王納拉姆辛在底格里斯河上游與扎格羅斯山麓一線擊潰自山區南下的盧盧比聯軍，奪回被劫掠的邊境關隘，把帝國北界重新推回山脈。軍隊骨幹仍是列陣持矛的步兵：卡面這件早王朝的埃及長矛，銅矛頭套在木桿上，與圓盾、銅盔同列，在狹窄山道上構成硬撼的矛牆。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 這場衝突是阿卡德王國與盧盧比山地聯盟之間的一場邊境戰爭，兩邊的組織形態截然不同。阿卡德一方是以阿卡德城為核心的中央王權，國王納拉姆辛同時握有統兵與祭祀的權力，軍隊由王室的常備兵、蘇美爾各城的民兵徵發兵，以及歸附的高地部眾組成，步兵為主幹，配以輕型四輪馬車作機動與指揮平台；薩爾貢在王璽上自述的五千四百人，是這一時期唯一留下數字的常備軍規模，納拉姆辛的軍隊應在同一數量級。盧盧比人沒有留下文字記載的國家機器，他們是扎格羅斯山區的部族聯盟，平日以小股步卒與駕馭野驢的斥候隊下山劫掠，遇到強敵才集結為遠征的大隊，沒有固定的都城，沒有王位繼承制，領軍的是各部落的頭人與戰時推舉的統帥；阿卡德文獻稱其為圖魯人，與同區的古提人、胡里安人在種族與語言上相近。戰場之外的第三方角色同樣要計入：南方的蘇美爾各城提供穀物與徵兵，東面的埃蘭是帝國之外最需提防的強權，而北方山地與沙漠地帶的游牧集團，時常趁阿卡德主力北征時擾動後方。
countriesEn: This clash was a frontier war between the Akkadian kingdom and a highland tribal confederation, and the two sides were organised in entirely different ways. On the Akkadian side stood a central kingship centred on the city of Akkad: King Naram-Sin held both the command of troops and the priestly office, and his army combined the royal standing force, militia levy from the Sumerian cities, and highland groups who had attached themselves to him. Infantry formed the core, supported by light four-wheeled chariots used for mobility and as a platform of command; the 5,400 men Sargon claimed on his royal seal is the only figure of this period that survives for the size of a standing army, and Naram-Sin's host was presumably of the same order of magnitude. The Lullubi had no documented state apparatus: they were a confederation of clans in the Zagros, normally raiding down in small bands of infantry and donkey-riding scouts, and only assembling into a large expeditionary column when a serious enemy forced them to; they had no fixed capital and no hereditary kingship, and their leaders were clan heads together with a war leader chosen for the occasion. Akkadian texts call them the Turu, a people closely related in race and language to the Gutians and Hurrians of the same uplands. Third parties outside the battlefield matter as well: the southern Sumerian cities supplied grain and levies, Elam to the east was the most dangerous extra-regional power, and the nomadic groups of the northern mountains and the deserts took advantage of an Akkadian main army in the north to raid the rear.
people: 納拉姆辛是這場戰爭的主角，阿卡德王朝第四位君主，薩爾貢之孫、瑪尼什圖蘇之子。他在位時把軍隊當中的神君稱號用在自己身上，這在美索不達米亞尚無先例；勝利石碑上，天上的月神薩恩以新月符號出現在他頭頂，說明這位國王已把自己的統治與神意直接掛鈎。留存下來的直接材料幾乎只有一件：現藏盧浮宮的納拉姆辛勝利石碑，銘文自誇自人類誕生以來沒有哪位國王毀滅過他的敵人，並把戰功歸於伊什塔拉的武器。碑面人物構成本戰爭唯一可考的目擊記錄：被長矛穿頸的盧盧比男子、矛鋒穿透面門的敗軍，以及被押到國王面前的盧盧比俘虜。盧盧比方面的統帥姓名不見於現存文獻，只能從作戰方式推測其為部落聯盟的戰時統帥，率隊自山區南下，直取阿卡德北境。他的父親瑪尼什圖蘇與祖父薩爾貢也都曾與同一批山地部族交鋒，納拉姆辛的戰役因此是三代人延續下來的同一條北境戰線；戰後他又把矛兵與車隊轉向東方與東北，去壓制阿摩利人與古提人。
peopleEn: Naram-Sin is the protagonist of this war, the fourth ruler of the Akkadian dynasty, grandson of Sargon and son of Manishtushu. During his reign he took for himself the title of divine ruler used within the army, a step without precedent in Mesopotamia; on the victory stele the moon god Sin appears above his head as a crescent, showing that the king had attached his rule directly to divine will. Almost the only direct material that survives is a single object: the Victory Stele of Naram-Sin in the Louvre, whose inscription boasts that since the creation of mankind no king had destroyed his enemies, and credits the work to the weapon of Ishtar. The figures carved on the stele are the only eyewitness record of the battle: a Lullubi man with a spear through his neck, a fallen enemy with the weapon driven into his face, and a Lullubi captive brought before the king. No name of the Lullubi commander survives in any text now known, so he can only be inferred from the mode of fighting, as a war leader of a tribal league who came down from the mountains to strike the northern Akkadian frontier. Naram-Sin's father Manishtushu and his grandfather Sargon had both fought the same mountain peoples, so this campaign was the third generation of a single continuing northern front; afterwards the king turned his spears and chariots eastward and north-eastward against the Amorites and the Gutians.
kits: 卡面這件埃及長矛屬於早王朝的典型形制：銅質矛頭以套筒綁在木桿上，柄尾加一枚尾錐，插地即可支撐掩護；它同時是守城兵器與野戰兵器，正是阿卡德步兵手裡的標準裝備。石碑上的阿卡德士兵裝備可以佐證：戴打磨發亮的銅盔，執矛、持斧、彎弓，胸前以圓形藤盾或嵌銅釦的盾牌遮護，身後的軍官執旗。盧盧比人一側的畫面則顯示他們裝備簡陋，僅有斧、矛與弓，沒有成建制的盾牌，頭髮散披、鬍鬚長，衣著以毛皮或粗麻為主。攻城與野戰的器材方面，阿卡德人有四輪實心車輪的輕型馬車，以驢或野驢拉動，車上載人與旗鼓，是戰場上的指揮中樞；破城用撞木與銅口工具，渡河用船。遠距補給靠天神的賜予：銅來自迪爾蒙與西奈，杉木來自地中海東岸的杉林，銅矛頭與木桿的更新都要依賴這條北方商路，而這條商路恰是盧盧比人年年下山的直接理由。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear on the card is a typical early dynastic form: a copper head socketed onto a wooden shaft, with a butt-spike added so that the weapon could be planted in the ground and braced; it served both to hold a wall and to fight in the open, and it was the standard weapon of the Akkadian infantryman. The equipment of the Akkadian soldiers described on the stele confirms this: they wear polished copper helmets, carry spears, axes and bows, and are covered at the chest by round wicker shields or shields with a copper boss, while officers behind them carry the standard. The Lullubi, by contrast, are shown with scant equipment, axes, spears and bows only, without formed shields, their hair loose and their beards long, dressed in hides or coarse linen. For siege and manoeuvre the Akkadians had light four-wheeled chariots with solid disc wheels, drawn by donkeys or onagers, carrying men, drums and standards, and serving as the command hub on the field; walls were broken with sledge-hammers and copper-tipped picks, and rivers crossed by boat. Long-distance supply rested on the favour of the gods: copper came from Dilmun and Sinai, cedar from the cedar forest on the eastern Mediterranean, and the renewal of copper heads and wooden hafts depended entirely on that northern trade road, which was precisely the reason the Lullubi came down year after year.
tactics: 這場戰役的戰術形象集中在石碑的構圖裡：國王站在山崖高處，軍隊在其下方以楔形向前推進，前鋒密集、縱深分層，越靠近國王行列越整齊，顯示的是以矛列陣、以車為鋒的打法。山地是關鍵地形：盧盧比人自高處下擊，居高臨下，阿卡德軍則利用山谷收攏縱隊，逐段推上斜坡，避免在開闊地被散兵游勇包圍。碑面所繪的網，一般被解釋為用來兜住潰退者的漁網，也有人認為是伊什塔拉的標幟，其軍事含義同樣是封住山道的退路。遠征的戰術素質表現在速度與紀律：隊伍脫離平原上的大城市，沿幼發拉河與卡班運渠北進，再翻越山脊直取盧盧比人的據點，使對方無法在平原上展開兵力；阿卡德軍還有以石斧、投石索壓制攀援者的手段，並用銅盔與密集盾陣抵擋高處射下的箭矢。勝負往往取決於某一條山道：奪下隘口，潰退的敵人就會順著谷地擁擠在狹窄道路上，被車陣與縱深步兵截斷。
tacticsEn: The tactical image of this battle is concentrated in the composition of the stele: the king stands on a rocky height, and below him the army advances in a wedge, the front dense and the files ranked in depth, the nearer the king the more regular the lines, which shows the doctrine of fighting in a line of spears with the chariot as the leading edge. The terrain is the decisive factor: the Lullubi struck down from the heights with the advantage of the slope, while the Akkadians closed up into narrow columns in the valleys and pushed up the inclines section by section, so as not to be surrounded in the open by scattered skirmishers. The net carved on the stele is generally read as a net for catching fugitives, though others take it for the emblem of Ishtar; its military meaning is the same either way, sealing the retreat through the mountain pass. The quality of the campaign lay in speed and discipline: the column left the great cities of the plain, moved north along the Euphrates and the King Canal, then crossed the ridges to strike the Lullubi strongholds, so that the enemy could never deploy in the plain. The Akkadians could also keep pressure on men climbing the slopes with stone axes and slings, and met the arrows raining from above with copper helmets and a close shield wall. Much turned on a single pass: once it was taken, the routed enemy jammed in the narrow valley road and was cut off by the chariots and the deep files of infantry.
data: 關於這場戰爭的數字，必須先說明紀年的分歧。蘇美爾王表諸抄本給納拉姆辛的年數約四十年，其在位起訖在中期、短期與長期三套年表之下相差一兩百年，因此前二二三〇年只是特定年表體系下的座標，而不是可以誤差在十年之內的確定年代。學界通常把這場戰役與四河之戰視為同一事件，而後者的斷代另有前二二五四與前二二七六等不同說法，這些差異源於年表體系的選擇，不是史料互相矛盾的結果；四河的地點一般被解作底格里斯河與其支流匯流的地帶，或指底格里斯河上游接近今土耳其邊界處的山谷。兵力方面沒有任何可靠數字可引：納拉姆辛的年名只留下對盧盧比人作戰的記載，並無兵員編製，可作量級參照的是薩爾貢王璽上的五千四百人。距離方面，軍隊自阿卡德或西帕拉出發，經底格里斯河上游向東北推進至扎格羅斯山麓，行程以數百公里計；作戰季節限於春末至初夏，冰雪消融使山道可行而山洪未至。本戰役的確切月份無文獻可考，卡面取四月，是按春汛退水、田事方興的傳統出征時令安排的。碑石本身近兩公尺高，以粉紅色石灰岩整塊雕成，一般認為原立於西帕拉，一九〇〇年在蘇薩的發掘中出土，今藏盧浮宮。
dataEn: The dating has to be settled first. Copies of the Sumerian King List give Naram-Sin about forty years on the throne, and the beginning and end of his reign fall in different places depending on whether the middle, short or long chronology is used, differing by a hundred or two hundred years; the year recorded for this battle, 2230 BC, therefore sits inside the dynastic sequence the list sets out, but at a fixed point of only one particular chronological system. Scholarship usually treats this campaign and the Battle of the Four Rivers as the same event, and that battle has been dated variously around 2254 BC or 2276 BC; the differences come from the choice of chronology, not from a contradiction in the sources. The Four Rivers are generally identified with the zone where the Tigris and its tributaries converge, or with the upper Tigris valley near the modern Turkish border. On the size of the forces no reliable figure survives: Naram-Sin's year-names record only that he campaigned against the Lullubi, without any establishment figures, and the only quantitative reference of the kind is the 5,400 men on Sargon's seal. As for distance, the column set out from Akkad or Sippar and moved north-east up the Tigris into the Zagros foothills, a march of several hundred kilometres; the campaigning season ran from late spring to early summer, when the snows had melted and the tracks were passable but the flash floods had not yet come. The exact month of the battle is not recorded; April is entered on the card as the traditional opening of the campaign season after the spring flood had receded. The stele itself stands nearly two metres high, carved from a single block of pink limestone, and is thought to have been erected originally at Sippar; it was excavated at Susa in 1900 and is now in the Louvre.
cause: 北境高地的部族與平原王國之間，本來就存在一條模糊而緊張的界線。盧盧比人居於扎格羅斯山地，過去控制著由伊朗高原通向美索不達米亞的幾條山道；阿卡德帝國的繁榮卻恰恰依賴這些山道帶來的物資：杉木、石料、銅礦、馬匹，以及北方部落的勞力。薩爾貢與瑪尼什圖蘇都曾把軍隊推上山路，但沒有一勞永逸地把高地壓服，於是每年的無事季節，部族便成群下山，襲破邊境關隘，驅走牲畜，劫走穀物，再退回山中。納拉姆辛面對的正是這一循環的第三次延續，他不能容忍帝國北境在最需要徵糧與徵兵的時候被反覆騷擾。促使他揮軍北上的直接契機，很可能是盧盧比聯軍的一次深入進攻擊潰了阿卡德的前線部隊，迫使國王御駕親征；石板上呈現的，與其說是一場遭遇戰，不如說是一次追擊與逆襲。宗教層面的理由同樣真實：納拉姆辛的王朝奉月神薩恩為守護神，北方山民所信奉的諸神則被他歸入異邦神；把這場戰爭寫成秩序與混亂的較量，是宮廷銘文有意為之的框架。
causeEn: Between the highland clans and the plains kingdom there ran a boundary that was always blurred and always tense. The Lullubi held the Zagros uplands and controlled several of the passes that led from the Iranian plateau into Mesopotamia; the prosperity of the Akkadian empire rested precisely on what came down those passes: cedar, stone, copper ore, horses, and the labour of the northern clans. Both Sargon and Manishtushu had driven armies up the mountain roads without ever putting the uplands permanently in order, so that in the idle season of each year the clans came down in bands, raided the frontier posts, drove off cattle, seized grain, and then withdrew again into the mountains. Naram-Sin was facing the third repetition of this cycle, and he could not tolerate the northern frontier of the empire being disturbed again at the moment when it needed its grain and its recruits. The immediate occasion for his march north was most likely a deep incursion by a Lullubi confederation that defeated an Akkadian forward force and forced the king to campaign in person; what the stele shows is less a meeting engagement than a pursuit and counter-stroke. The religious ground was equally real: Naram-Sin's dynasty served the moon god Sin as its guardian, while the gods of the mountain folk were counted among the foreign deities; writing the war up as a contest between order and confusion was a framing the court scribes deliberately chose.
impact: 這場戰役的結果，最終以一件石頭留在了今天：盧浮宮的納拉姆辛勝利石碑。碑面所確立的三件事，後來都成了兩河流域的通例。第一，國王的形像在整幅構圖中大於所有士兵，採用的是尊者加大的等級比例，而非依人體比例的寫實；這是美索不達米亞紀念碑藝術的一次根本轉向，後來巴比倫與亞述的凱旋浮雕都沿此路徑。第二，月神的新月符號與伊什塔拉的鷹徽被刻在戰功之上，國王第一次以神授的語言書寫自己的勝利，四境之王這頂頭銜也自此出現，帝國的觀念被寫進了石頭。第三，雕刻的母題本身，國王居高臨下、敵軍在腳下潰散，成為後世亞述王凱旋浮雕的直接藍本；連同此後數百年阿卡德諸王、沙爾卡利沙瑞與古巴比倫諸王的勝利石碑一起，構成亞述宮廷藝術的參照系。另一層影響是負面的：帝國沒有解決北方問題。盧盧比人並未被打散，紮根於山地的部族聯盟在整個第三千紀持續存在，烏爾第三王朝的烏爾納姆、舒爾吉等人仍須一再北上征討；而在阿卡德王朝末年，正是同一片山區的另一批部族，古提人，攻入平原，終結了這個王朝。納拉姆辛的勝利因此是一場把問題推後而不是解決的勝利。
impactEn: The outcome of this campaign survives today in a single stone: the Victory Stele of Naram-Sin in the Louvre. Three things established on that stone later became common practice across Mesopotamia. First, the king's figure is larger than every soldier in the composition, using the hierarchical scale of the superior rather than naturalistic proportion; this was a fundamental turn in Mesopotamian monumental art, and the victory reliefs of Babylonia and Assyria followed the same path. Second, the crescent of the moon god and the eagle emblem of Ishtar were carved above the victory, the king wrote his triumph for the first time in the language of divine grant, and the title king of the four quarters appears; the idea of empire was written into stone. Third, the motif itself, the king standing above and the enemy scattering below, became the direct model for the Assyrian victory reliefs, and together with the stelae of the Akkadian kings, of Shar-kali-sharri and of the Old Babylonian sovereigns it formed the reference set for Assyrian court art. There is a darker side to the effect as well: the empire did not solve the northern question. The Lullubi were not scattered; the tribal league rooted in the mountains existed throughout the third millennium, and Ur-Nammu and Shulgi of the Third Dynasty of Ur still had to campaign north again and again. At the end of the Akkadian dynasty it was another people from those same highlands, the Gutians, who came down into the plain and ended the dynasty. Naram-Sin's victory was therefore a victory that postponed the problem rather than solving it.
result: 以盧盧比人為對手的戰役，最後以阿卡德方的完全勝利告終。盧盧比聯軍被擊潰在山谷之中，退路被截斷，殘部翻越山脊退入高地的據點；石板上被長矛穿頸的散兵與被押送的俘虜，是這場勝利的兩個定格畫面。國王把軍隊推進山區本身，而不是只守在平原上的界線，奪下山地通道後，阿卡德的商隊重新可以北上採購杉木與銅料，帝國北境的稅源與徵兵線恢復正常。納拉姆辛本人藉此把自己的統治寫成神意所賜，在軍隊中被當作神來崇拜，並首稱四境之王，把阿卡德從一個仍帶城邦聯盟色彩的王國，變成自稱統治整個已知世界的帝國。戰後他仍要應付四方：南方蘇美爾各城的忠誠需要安撫，東方埃蘭仍是威脅，北方與東北的古提人、阿摩利人不斷南侵。帝國的壽命並沒有因這場勝利而延長；納拉姆辛死後，其子沙爾卡利沙瑞在位二十六年，王朝終於在北方壓力下崩潰。總結這一場：阿卡德靠著密集的矛陣、車隊與嚴整的後勤在山地把高地部族打散，贏得一場足以寫進石頭的勝利，卻把真正的北境問題留給了後人。
resultEn: The war against the Lullubi ended in a complete victory for the Akkadian side. The Lullubi confederacy was broken in the valley, its retreat cut off, and the survivors pushed back over the ridges into the highland strongholds; the man with a spear through his neck and the captive led before the king are the two frozen images of that victory. The king drove his army into the mountains rather than merely holding the line on the plain, and once the mountain passes were taken the Akkadian caravans could go north again to buy cedar and copper, restoring the normal flow of the empire's northern revenue and of its recruits. Naram-Sin used the occasion to write his own rule as granted by the gods, was worshipped as a god within the army, and first took the title king of the four quarters, turning Akkad from a kingdom still carrying features of a city-state league into a state claiming to rule the whole known world. Even afterwards he had to answer on all four sides: the loyalty of the southern Sumerian cities had to be managed, Elam remained a threat in the east, and the Gutians and Amorites pressed in from the north and north-east. The empire did not live longer for the victory; after Naram-Sin died his son Shar-kali-sharri reigned for twenty-six years, and the dynasty finally collapsed under northern pressure. Summing this up: Akkad broke the highland clans with dense spear lines, chariots and strict logistics, winning a victory worthy of being carved in stone, and passed the real problem of the northern frontier on to those who came after.
